column1: In FastAPI, what happens if you call blocking I/O (e.g. time.sleep) inside an {{c1::async def}} endpoint?
column2: It freezes the {{c2::main Event Loop thread}}, blocking all other concurrent users.

column1: Why is a plain {{c1::def}} endpoint in FastAPI safe from blocking the event loop?
column2: FastAPI automatically executes plain def functions in an {{c2::external threadpool}}.

column1: Why are {{c1::async/await coroutines}} significantly lighter than OS threads for 1,000+ requests?
column2: Coroutines run on {{c2::a single thread}} using cooperative pauses, whereas OS threads each cost {{c3::MBs of stack memory and context-switching}}.

column1: For CPU-bound tasks in FastAPI (e.g. matrix multiplication), why should you NOT use {{c1::async def}}?
column2: Because CPU tasks don't yield via await, {{c2::freezing the single Event Loop thread}} completely.

column1: FastAPI: لماذا تجمد دالة async def السيرفر عند تنفيذ عمليات CPU-bound ثقيلة، وما الحل؟
column2:
السبب: كود CPU-bound لا يحتوي على await فيحتكر الـ Event Loop الوحيد ويمنع معالجة الطلبات الأخرى.
الحل: استخدام def عادية (يرسلها FastAPI إلى Threadpool) أو ProcessPoolExecutor لتجاوز الـ GIL.
